discovery: Prediction and discovery of kilonovae, establishing neutron-star mergers as a cosmic site of r-process heavy-element nucleosynthesis

nominees.name: Brian D. Metzger
nominees.affiliation: Columbia University and Flatiron Institute, USA

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

subfield: Astrophysics (time-domain and multi-messenger astronomy, nuclear astrophysics)
motivation: Where the heaviest elements, such as gold and platinum, were made was a long-standing open question. Metzger developed the first quantitative model of the 'kilonova', a thermal transient powered by the radioactive decay of freshly synthesised r-process nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta. Kasen showed that lanthanide opacities make these transients red and long-lived, which told observers what to look for. In 2013 Tanvir led the detection of a near-infrared kilonova after the short GRB 130603B. This was the first observational evidence linking short gamma-ray bursts, compact-object mergers and r-process production. The predictions were confirmed in detail by AT2017gfo, the optical and infrared counterpart of GW170817, whose light curve and spectra matched the models. Together these results opened multi-messenger astronomy beyond gravitational waves alone. They also explained the origin of a large part of the periodic table and gave a new route to measuring cosmic expansion.
